name: Black Rock Desert National Conservation Area BLM Free Primitive Camping

management_agency.name: Bureau of Land Management - Winnemucca District

rules_and_regulations.cost: 100% Free - No fees, no permits required for primitive dispersed camping on BLM land (excluding fee closure window during Burning Man event)
rules_and_regulations.stay_limit: 14 consecutive days max stay within 28-day period
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Dispersed primitive camping permitted throughout the 1.2-million-acre Black Rock Desert High Rock Canyon NCA. Do not drive on wet playa.

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Playa mud / desert alkali soil: full human waste pack-out using portable toilet or WAG bags strictly required on playa surface. Deep cat-hole 6 inches deep in upland sandy soil 200ft from hot springs.
waste_disposal_rules.trash_policy: Strict Leave No Trace pack-it-in pack-it-out. Zero trash collection on playa.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Bring your own firewood. Gathering sagebrush or playa vegetation strictly prohibited.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Campfires must be contained in elevated metal fire pans. Never ignite fires directly on playa clay (causes permanent fire scars).

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Paved state highway to unpaved flat alkali playa lakebed / gravel washboard roads (NV-347 / Soldier Meadows Road)
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Flat smooth dry playa when dry; turns into liquid mud when wet (vehicles freeze in place). Gravel side roads have sharp volcanic rocks.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: High clearance car or 4x4 recommended (Normal low clearance 2WD cars can drive on dry playa near Gerlach access points with caution)

nomad_connectivity_rating.verizon_reliability: 2-3 bars 4G LTE near Gerlach access point; 0-1 bar on open playa
nomad_connectivity_rating.att_reliability: 1-2 bars 4G LTE near main highway corridor
nomad_connectivity_rating.terrain_obstruction_risk: Low (Vast flat alkali desert valley bounded by Calico & Jackson mountain ranges)

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: 55-70°F, high wind storms, wet playa sections, hot spring soaks.
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: Hot (95-105°F), intense desert sun, dust storms (whiteout dust devils), 100% dry playa.
seasonal_weather_effects.fall: Ideal boondocking season (65-80°F daytime, 35-45°F nights), low wind, clear skies.
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: Cold High Desert winter (30-45°F daytime, 10-25°F nights), mud on playa.

dangers_and_hazards: Getting stuck in wet alkali mud (towing costs exceed $1,500 in remote desert)
Whiteout dust storms with 50+ mph wind gusts
Extreme isolation: no cell service, water, or gas for 50+ miles
High thermal temperature hot springs (scalding water hazard)

common_human_made_sounds: Infrequent high-speed land vehicles on open playa

human_demographics_and_culture: Off-grid nomads, rockhounds, hot spring enthusiasts, amateur astronomers, high-speed land record teams, and overlanders.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: Northern Paiute indigenous traditions honor the Black Rock Desert and Hot Springs as sacred domains of the water and fire spirits.
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: Profound silent desert energy, vast void spatial clearance, pristine Bortle 1 night sky.

nearby_hiking_trails.trail_name: High Rock Canyon National Historic Trail
nearby_hiking_trails.features: Deep volcanic canyon walls, emigrant wagon trail inscriptions

public_reviews_summary: One of the most surreal and vast primitive camping expanses in North America. Absolute silence and infinite horizons. Starlink mandatory for remote internet.
other_data: Bortle Class 1 night sky (darkest skies in USA). 100% solar efficiency.
